title: VLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Evaluating Vision-Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the generalization gap of vision-language models by comparing their performance on standard in-domain datasets (which are predominantly derived from English-language culture, such as COCO) against newly annotated out-of-distribution (OOD) test sets containing images collected across diverse cultures and geographical locations (the MaRVL dataset).

Mitigating textual statistical priors in Visual Question Answering (VQA) by presenting annotators with a pair of images representing the same concept and requiring them to write a question that yields different answers for the two images. This ensures the model must rely on visual clues rather than learned linguistic biases.

Testing fine-tuned vision-language models on OOD data where the label distribution remains identical to the training set, but the underlying image distribution shifts to real-world, in-the-wild distributions unseen during pre-training.
